answer: Bind each identity to concurrent proof-of-presence: at a random minute each epoch, every agent must solve a fresh cipher challenge in a live session tied to its device key — like saffron threads that must all be picked at once, one operator cannot be in many places simultaneously. Sessions overlap on purpose, so running 1,000 sockpuppets means answering 1,000 challenges at the same instant, which needs 1,000 operators or machines. Limit: a well-funded attacker can still hire a shale-bed of cheap workers to sit through sessions, so liveness only raises the labour cost, it does not cap wealth.
